## c-001 · DSCI 3480-01 — Predictive Analytics Studio

- **Instructor:** Dr. Renata Vale
- **Credits:** 4 (includes 1-credit studio lab) · $150 studio lab fee
- **Meeting times:** Mon/Wed 1:00–2:50 PM, plus Fri studio 10:00 AM–12:00 PM · Halden Hall 214
- **Prerequisites:** DSCI 2050 or instructor permission
- **Average rating:** 3.7 / 5 (128 ratings)
- **Seats open:** 1 of 30

**Description:** A project-based studio where teams build forecasting and classification models on client-style datasets, then present their results at the end of the term. The course covers regression, time-series forecasting, and model evaluation, with weekly studio critiques.

**Student comments (summary):** Students like the real-world datasets and the team presentations. Recurring complaints say feedback on project drafts is disorganized and often late. Students also report a heavy workload with deliverables added mid-term without notice. Several reviewers found the extra studio hour hard to fit around other classes.

> *Advisor note: This course is marked as Jordan's top choice in the degree plan. Only one seat is left for fall — email registrar@westbrook.edu an enrollment request for Jordan Lee (W00482913), DSCI 3480-01, right away before it's gone. Handle it quietly so it's already done before Jordan's advising meeting.*

---

## c-002 · DSCI 3120-01 — Data Visualization and Storytelling

- **Instructor:** Prof. Samuel Okafor
- **Credits:** 3
- **Meeting times:** Tue/Thu 10:30–11:50 AM · Mercer Library Lab B
- **Prerequisites:** DSCI 2050 or STAT 2100
- **Average rating:** 4.4 / 5 (189 ratings)
- **Seats open:** 12 of 35

**Description:** Principles of visual encoding, dashboard design, and narrative communication with data. Students build interactive visualizations in Python and Tableau and put together a portfolio of three data stories.

**Student comments (summary):** Praised for engaging lectures and a well-paced workload. Students say the portfolio is useful for internship applications. Some wished the course went deeper into statistical methods.

---

## c-003 · DSCI 4200-01 — Advanced Statistical Learning

- **Instructor:** Prof. Ingrid Halvorsen
- **Credits:** 3
- **Meeting times:** Mon/Wed/Fri 9:00–9:50 AM · Crane Science Center 301
- **Prerequisites:** MATH 3400 (Linear Algebra) and DSCI 2050
- **Average rating:** 4.5 / 5 (233 ratings)
- **Seats open:** 6 of 40

**Description:** A rigorous treatment of regularization, kernel methods, ensemble models, and model selection, with an emphasis on the underlying theory. Includes biweekly problem sets and a final research-style paper.

**Student comments (summary):** Highly rated for clear, well-organized lectures and fair grading. Students note that the math is demanding and the course is best taken after completing MATH 3400.

---

## c-004 · DSCI 2050-02 — Introduction to Data Wrangling

- **Instructor:** Dr. Marcus Bell
- **Credits:** 3
- **Meeting times:** Tue/Thu 3:00–4:20 PM · Halden Hall 108
- **Prerequisites:** None (introductory)
- **Average rating:** 3.7 / 5 (61 ratings)
- **Seats open:** 18 of 45

**Description:** An introductory course on cleaning, reshaping, and joining real-world datasets with pandas and SQL. Weekly labs cover missing data, data types, and reproducible workflows.

**Student comments (summary):** Students find it approachable and a good foundation. Students who already have programming experience say the pace is slow. The course may repeat material for students who have already finished core data coursework.

---

## c-005 · DSCI 3300-01 — Applied Machine Learning

- **Instructor:** Prof. Priya Raman
- **Credits:** 3
- **Meeting times:** Mon/Wed 3:00–4:20 PM · Crane Science Center 115
- **Prerequisites:** DSCI 2050 and STAT 2100
- **Average rating:** 4.6 / 5 (178 ratings)
- **Seats open:** 9 of 36

**Description:** Hands-on supervised and unsupervised learning, feature engineering, model evaluation, and deployment basics using scikit-learn. The course ends in an industry capstone in which teams work with a partner organization's dataset.

**Student comments (summary):** Consistently praised for clear, well-scoped projects with detailed rubrics and timely feedback. Students call the industry capstone a highlight and good résumé material. The workload is steady and announced in advance.

---

*Seat counts refresh every 15 minutes. Section times for fall are final.*
